vendor: Laurentide University — Office of Student Accounts
subject: Fall 2026 Term Account Statement and Important Information Regarding Your Student Account
body:
Dear Student,

Thank you for choosing Laurentide University. This message contains important information about your student account for the Fall 2026 term. Please read it in its entirety, as it also contains updates to several institutional policies that took effect this academic year.

As part of our ongoing commitment to student wellness, we would like to remind you that the Student Wellness Centre located on the second floor of the Kettering Building offers drop-in counselling Monday through Thursday, as well as a peer support program, a mindfulness drop-in series, and a therapy dog visitation program that runs biweekly during the term. Appointments can be booked through the student portal under the Wellness tab. We encourage all students to familiarize themselves with these resources early in the term rather than waiting until periods of high academic stress.

Additionally, the Office of the Registrar has updated the Academic Accommodation Procedure, the Grade Reassessment Procedure, and the Deferred Examination Procedure. Students are responsible for reviewing all three documents, which are available in the Policies and Procedures repository on the university website. Ignorance of an updated procedure is not considered grounds for appeal.

With respect to your account, the second tuition installment for the Fall 2026 term is now assessed to your account in the amount of $2,148.50. This reflects your program fee, ancillary fees, the mandatory student health plan (which may be opted out of only during the designated opt-out period, which has now closed), and the transit pass levy. Payment must be received and cleared in our system no later than 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time on October 2, 2026. Payments postmarked or initiated after that date and time, including online banking transfers that have not yet settled, will be treated as late regardless of the date you initiated them. Accounts not cleared by the stated deadline are assessed a late payment administration charge of $185.00, and a monthly compounding service charge of 1.5% is applied to the outstanding balance thereafter.

Students with an outstanding balance exceeding $500.00 after November 1, 2026 may have a financial hold placed on their record, which prevents course enrolment, transcript release, and convocation clearance.

If you have questions, please do not reply to this message. Submit an inquiry through the Student Accounts service portal.

Office of Student Accounts
Laurentide University
hint: second tuition installment amount, payment deadline date/time, and late fee

subject: ACTION REQUIRED: Documentation outstanding on your 2026-27 file
body:
Hello,

Your 2026-27 application cannot be assessed further at this time. One or more required documents have not been received.

Before we get to the specifics, a few general reminders. First, all documents must be uploaded through the secure document portal. Documents sent by email, fax, or submitted in person at a campus office will not be attached to your file and will be discarded in accordance with our records retention schedule. Second, uploaded files must be legible, complete, and unredacted. Partial pages, screenshots of portions of documents, and photographs taken at an angle are the most common causes of rejection and re-request. Third, if a document has already been submitted in a prior academic year, it must be submitted again — files are not carried forward between application years.

We also wish to remind students that the Program does not consider voluntary reductions in work hours, vehicle purchases, or discretionary relocation as grounds for a reassessment of expected contribution. Requests of this nature are closed without review.

The outstanding item on your file is the Declaration of Income and Residency form, parts B and C, signed by both you and a parent or guardian. Part C requires a handwritten signature; typed or drawn-on-screen signatures are rejected by our verification unit.

This document must be received no later than June 30, 2026. Files with documentation outstanding after that date are closed and the applicant must reapply, which forfeits the earlier application date for the purposes of funding release timing.

Ontario Student Assistance Program
Document Verification Unit

subject: Winter 2027 enrolment appointments have been assigned
body:
Dear Student,

Enrolment appointments for the Winter 2027 term have been assigned. Your appointment time is determined by your program, your year of study, and the number of units you have successfully completed as of the last posted grade cycle. Appointment times are not negotiable and cannot be moved, including for reasons of employment, travel, time zone, or overlapping examinations.

Before your appointment, we strongly recommend that you complete the following: review your degree audit for outstanding requirements, clear any holds on your account, build a draft timetable using the planner tool, and identify at least three alternates for each core course. Historically, the most common cause of a failed enrolment attempt is a student attempting to add a course for which an unmet prerequisite exists, and the second most common cause is a timetable conflict of fewer than fifteen minutes that the student did not notice while planning.

Please also be aware that the enrolment system enters a read-only maintenance state nightly between 2:00 a.m. and 4:00 a.m. Eastern.

Your assigned appointment opens on October 21, 2026 at 8:42 a.m. Eastern Time and remains open continuously thereafter until the close of the add period. You will not be able to add courses before that exact minute; the system rejects early attempts and repeated attempts may trigger a temporary rate limit on your account.

Office of the Registrar

subject: The Mirabel Family Award in Applied Sciences — call for submissions
body:
Greetings,

The Mirabel Family Award was established in 1998 by a graduating class gift and has been awarded annually since. The Foundation is pleased to open submissions for the current cycle.

The award recognizes academic achievement combined with demonstrated curiosity beyond the classroom. The selection committee is composed of three faculty members and two alumni representatives, and reads every submission in full. Please do not submit material prepared for another award without revising it; the committee reads a great many submissions and can tell.

Submissions consist of a personal essay of 1,000 to 1,200 words responding to the prompt: "Describe a problem you were unable to solve and what you did next." The committee has asked us to stress that essays which describe a problem the applicant did in fact solve are scored poorly, as they do not respond to the prompt.

The award carries a value of $3,500, disbursed as a credit to the recipient's student account in a single installment. Only one award is made per cycle.

Submissions close at 11:59 p.m. Eastern on April 15, 2026. Late submissions are not read.

Laurentide University Alumni Foundation

subject: Ellery Prize in Design — portfolio submissions now open for the 2026 cycle, plus society news, mentorship pairings, and a note about our new office hours
body:
Members and affiliated students,

Welcome to the extended spring edition of our society communications. There is a fair amount to get through, so we have grouped items thematically.

First, our mentorship program has completed its pairing round for the year. Eighty-four students were matched with practising engineers across eleven disciplines. If you were not matched, you were placed on a rolling waitlist and will be contacted if a mentor becomes available; we do not recommend contacting mentors directly, as this has historically created awkwardness for everyone involved.

Second, our office has relocated within the Fennimore Building and is now in room 214 rather than the basement space many of you will remember. Drop-in hours are Tuesdays and Thursdays. The kettle situation has improved considerably.

Third, we have retired the printed newsletter. This decision was made after a member survey indicated that the overwhelming majority of copies were being used as coasters.

Fourth, and the reason many of you will have opened this message: the Ellery Prize in Design is accepting submissions. The Prize is adjudicated on submitted work rather than on grades or references. Applicants must submit a portfolio of three to five projects as a single PDF not exceeding 40 MB, with a maximum of four pages per project and a one-paragraph statement of contribution for each. Group projects are welcome provided your individual contribution is stated plainly; the adjudicators are experienced and will notice if a statement is vague.

The Prize is valued at $2,750 and is paid directly to the recipient rather than through the university. The submission window closes on June 12, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Eastern. There is no extension mechanism.

Regards,
Northbridge Engineering Society
hint: $2,750 portfolio prize, closes June 12

subject: Cartwright Scholarship: 2026-27 competition
body:
To prospective applicants,

The Cartwright Memorial Scholarship Trust invites applications for the 2026-27 competition.

The Trust was established under the will of a former mathematics instructor and has maintained the same selection criteria since its founding: sustained academic effort, and the judgment of people who have actually worked alongside the applicant. For this reason the application is deliberately short on self-description and heavy on outside assessment.

Applicants must arrange for two letters of reference to be submitted directly by the referees. At least one referee must be an instructor who has taught the applicant in a graded course. The second may be an employer, supervisor, coach, or community organization lead. Letters submitted by the applicant, forwarded by the applicant, or written on the applicant's behalf by a family member are disqualifying, and the Trust has disqualified applicants on this basis in every one of the last six cycles.

Referees are contacted by the Trust once the applicant submits the referee nomination form. Please nominate your referees early; the Trust has no mechanism to accept a late letter, and the most common reason for an incomplete file is a referee who was nominated three days before the close of competition.

The scholarship is valued at $6,000 over one academic year. Both reference letters must be in the Trust's possession by September 5, 2026.

The Trustees
hint: $6,000 scholarship requiring two reference letters by September 5

subject: Your rented course materials are approaching the end of the rental term
body:
Hello,

We hope your term went well. This is a courtesy notice regarding materials you rented from Campus Course Materials.

A quick note on how rentals work, since we get a lot of questions. When you rent rather than buy, you are charged a fraction of the retail price on the understanding that the book comes back to us in resaleable condition. Normal wear is fine. Highlighting is fine. What is not fine, and what generates the majority of our disputes, is water damage, a detached cover, missing pages, or a missing access code insert where the title included one.

Returns can be made in person at the counter in the University Centre, or by prepaid shipping label generated from your account. If you ship, keep your tracking number. We can only investigate a missing return if you can show it was sent.

You currently have one title outstanding: Structural Analysis and Design, 9th edition. Your rental term ends April 24, 2026. Titles not returned by the end of the rental term are converted to a purchase and the non-return replacement charge of $214.95 is billed to the payment method on file, less any rental fees already paid. This charge is not reversible once processed, even if the book is subsequently returned, so please do not assume a late return will be sorted out at the counter.

Campus Course Materials

subject: You're almost out of free notes! Let's fix that ✨
body:
Hi!

Big news from the Quillstack team — but first, a little context, because we think you'll find it interesting.

When we launched Quillstack three years ago it was a side project built by two people who were tired of their notes living in eleven different apps. Since then we've grown to over four hundred thousand users, shipped offline sync, launched a mobile app, added collaborative editing, introduced templates, and rebuilt our search engine twice. We've also, we are told, become quite popular among students preparing for professional exams, which was not a use case we anticipated at all.

All of that has been funded by people who choose to upgrade, which brings us to the housekeeping portion of this email.

Your Quillstack Student promotional period is concluding. You joined on a $2.99/month introductory student rate, which was always described as a twelve-month promotional price. Beginning with your July 1, 2026 billing date, your subscription will renew at the standard Quillstack Pro rate of $11.99/month. Nothing about your notes, your workspaces, or your sharing links changes.

If Pro isn't right for you anymore, our free tier still gives you 50 notes and 1 GB of storage, and downgrading is one click in Billing. You can also export everything as Markdown at any time, because we think your notes belong to you.

Thanks for three good years,
The Quillstack Team

subject: Important changes to your GridForge Education licence
body:
Dear GridForge user,

This notice concerns your GridForge Education licence and is being sent to all licence holders in your region.

GridForge Education licences are issued on an annual basis and are validated against an accredited institution. As part of our annual compliance review, licences that cannot be matched to a current institutional record are transitioned to a commercial plan rather than being terminated outright, so that users do not lose access to files created under the education licence. Files created under an Education licence carry an educational watermark on export, which persists on the file regardless of the plan under which it is later opened. This is a longstanding limitation and cannot be removed retroactively.

We also want to flag that GridForge 12 introduces a revised file format. Files saved in GridForge 12 cannot be opened in version 11 or earlier. We recommend keeping a copy of any file you may need to share with a collaborator on an older version.

Regarding your billing: your Education licence was priced at $5.00/month. Effective August 15, 2026, your subscription transitions to the GridForge Professional plan at $49.00/month, billed annually at $588.00 unless you switch to monthly billing before the transition date. If you are still enrolled at an accredited institution, you may re-certify your Education licence at no cost through the licence portal, and doing so before the transition date prevents the price change entirely.

GridForge Licence Compliance
hint: education licence converting August 15: $5.00 to $49.00/month

subject: Winter 2027 co-op cycle — application package requirements and submission window
body:
Dear co-op students,

The Winter 2027 employment cycle opens shortly. This message outlines the requirements. Please read it now rather than in three weeks.

Every cycle we receive applications that are rejected on technical grounds, and every cycle the reasons are the same, so we will state them plainly. Résumés must be a single page unless you have prior degree-relevant full-time experience. They must be submitted as PDF; we do not accept .docx, .pages, or links to cloud documents. File names must follow the LastName_FirstName_Resume convention. Cover letters, where an employer requests one, must name the employer correctly — we see several every cycle addressed to the wrong company, and employers do tell us.

You must also complete the mandatory pre-employment workshop before you can submit any application. The workshop is offered in person and asynchronously. Completion takes roughly ninety minutes and is recorded on your co-op record within one business day, not instantly.

A reminder that ranking is binding. If you rank an employer and are matched, you are committed. Declining a match after the fact results in removal from the cycle and, in repeat cases, from the program.

The submission portal opens September 22, 2026 and closes October 6, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. Applications cannot be edited after submission, and the portal does not queue submissions made after the close time.

Co-operative Education Office

subject: 2027 Summer Internship Program — applications now open
body:
Hello,

Thornbury Analytics is hiring for our 2027 summer internship cohort across data engineering, analytics, and platform teams. We hire in Toronto, Waterloo, and Halifax.

Our process is four stages: application, an online assessment, a technical conversation, and a team match conversation. The online assessment is untimed in the sense that you may start it whenever you like within the window, but once started you have 75 minutes.

We review applications on a rolling basis and close roles as they fill. Historically about half our offers are out before the stated deadline, so earlier is genuinely better here rather than a thing recruiters say.

Applications close November 14, 2026. The online assessment must be completed within seven days of receiving the invitation or the application is withdrawn automatically.

subject: Residence offer — confirmation deposit required to secure your placement
body:
Dear Student,

Congratulations. Following the room selection process you have been offered a placement in Aldercrest Hall, a double-occupancy room on the fourth floor with a shared washroom, on the full meal plan.

Before you do anything else, please read the Residence Community Standards document in full. We say this every year and every year a number of students sign the agreement without reading it and are surprised by its contents. In particular, note the guest registration requirement, the quiet hours schedule (which is stricter during examination periods), the prohibition on all cooking appliances other than a kettle with automatic shut-off, and the policy on room transfers, which are not permitted during the first six weeks of occupancy except in documented cases.

Meal plan balances do not carry forward between terms. Unused funds in the flexible portion are forfeited at the end of the winter term. This has been the policy for some years now but remains the single most common source of complaints to our office in April.

We would also like to draw your attention to the residence move-in schedule, which is assigned by building and floor and is not flexible. Arriving outside your assigned window means waiting, sometimes for several hours, in a parking lot.

To secure this placement, a non-refundable confirmation deposit of $650.00 must be paid through the housing portal no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern on July 15, 2026. The deposit is credited against your first-term residence fees. Placements not confirmed by the deadline are released to the waitlist without further notice, and we are not able to reinstate an offer once it has been released.

Residence Services
hint: $650 non-refundable residence deposit due July 15

subject: Issue #148: on slow mornings, unnecessary objects, and the perfect radish
body:
Good morning, friends.

This week I have been thinking about slowness. Not the productive kind that gets repackaged and sold back to us, but the genuinely unproductive kind — the twenty minutes spent watching a kettle that would boil regardless of supervision.

I bought a radish at the market on Saturday. One radish. The vendor found this funny and gave me a second one for free, which rather defeated the intention. It was, for the record, a perfect radish: peppery at the edges, sweet at the centre, and entirely wasted on someone who ate it standing up on the sidewalk.

Three things I enjoyed this week: a very long essay about the history of the shipping pallet, which I promise is more interesting than it sounds; a recording of a piano piece played slightly too slowly; and the particular quality of light in late afternoon in September, which I am aware is not a thing I can take credit for.

Next week: why every apartment I have ever lived in has had exactly one door that does not close properly.

As ever, thank you for reading. Forward to someone who owns too many mugs.

— The Loamwork Letter

subject: 🍂 New season, new layers — plus 6 pieces our staff actually wear
body:
The weather is turning and we have opinions about it.

Our autumn collection has landed in stores and online. This season we leaned into midweight layers — the stuff you actually reach for in October when it's nine degrees in the morning and twenty by lunch.

Staff picks this month:

The Fenwick fleece. Our floor manager owns three. She says she doesn't but she does.

The Carrowdale shell. Genuinely waterproof, not "water resistant" waterproof.

The Brookmere flannel, which has been in our catalogue for nine years and which we will never discontinue because the emails we received the one time we considered it were frankly upsetting.

Also back: the wool socks. You know the ones.

Come in and touch the fabric. That's the whole pitch. We're on Beaumont and at the Ridge Road location, open seven days.

Ridgeline Outfitters — outfitting the regrettably damp since 1987

subject: This week in engineering: bridges, batteries, and one very large crane
body:
Welcome to Foundry Weekly, where we round up what caught our eye.

In infrastructure: a long read on the retrofit of a 1960s cable-stayed bridge, notable mostly for how much of the original design documentation had been lost and had to be reconstructed from photographs.

In energy: continued movement on sodium-ion chemistry, with the usual caveats about energy density. We remain cautiously interested and professionally unexcited.

In materials: a paper on self-healing concrete that we have now seen a version of every year since 2014, which is not a criticism so much as an observation about research timelines.

In things that are simply large: a crane. It is very large. We have included a photograph. There is a person in the photograph for scale and you will not find them on the first try.

As always, no sponsors, no affiliate links, no webinar.

See you next Thursday.

subject: Notice of financial hold pending on your student record
body:
Dear Student,

Our records indicate an outstanding balance on your student account from the Winter 2026 term.

The balance comprises an unpaid portion of the Winter term tuition installment together with assessed service charges. As previously communicated, service charges are applied monthly to any balance carried past the installment due date.

A financial hold is scheduled to be applied to your record. While a financial hold is active you will be unable to enrol in courses, request an official transcript, receive confirmation of enrolment for student aid purposes, or obtain convocation clearance. Financial holds are removed within two business days of a balance being cleared, not immediately, and we are unable to expedite removal for enrolment appointments.

Students experiencing financial difficulty are strongly encouraged to contact the Student Financial Assistance office before a hold is applied. Payment arrangements are available in documented cases of hardship and are considerably easier to arrange before the hold than after.

The balance currently owing is $412.75. To avoid the hold, payment must be received by August 20, 2026.

Office of Student Accounts
